title: New Netherland
capsule: New Netherland (Nieuw-Nederland) was a Dutch Republic colony on the northeast coast of North America, run by the Dutch West India Company from 1624 as a chartered settlement colony after earlier fur-trading voyages, centered on New Amsterdam at the southern tip of Manhattan. At its height it claimed territory from the South (Delaware) River to the Fresh (Connecticut) River, encompassing the Hudson valley, parts of Long Island, and outposts in present-day New Jersey and Delaware. English forces under Colonel Richard Nicolls entered New Amsterdam harbor on 27 August 1664 and Director-General Peter Stuyvesant surrendered without a fight; the colony was renamed New York. The Dutch briefly retook it in 1673 during the Third Anglo-Dutch War but permanently ceded sovereignty in the 1674 Treaty of Westminster.
attestation: Boundaries from Seshat Cliopatria (Bennett et al., Scientific Data 2025; CC BY 4.0), digitized from standard historical atlases at ~0.07° resolution. The core Hudson valley and Manhattan settlement of New Netherland is very well attested through Dutch colonial records, but the claimed boundaries toward the Connecticut River and into Delaware overlapped with English territorial claims and were disputed throughout the colony's existence.
